patterns.name: Unpunctuated complete wh-/yes-no questions (no fillers)
patterns.explanation: Clean, self-contained questions with no trailing '?' are predicted unfinished, e.g. 'what happens if I miss a dose of the antibiotic', 'how long am I supposed to keep icing my knee', 'which pharmacy did the prescription get sent to', 'How often do performance reviews happen and what do they entail', 'sorry what do you mean by persistent'. The model seems to wait for a '?' token. It hasn't learned that a question word followed by a complete clause (subject + verb + all required arguments) is a terminal shape even without punctuation.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~400 contrastive pairs and triplets of spoken questions in medical, HR, travel and tech domains, all lowercase and with no final punctuation. (a) The complete question, labelled finished ('how soon can I go back to running after a sprain like this'). (b) The same question cut inside a clause, labelled unfinished ('how soon can I go back to', 'which pharmacy did the'). (c) The same question with '?' added, labelled finished. Include questions that end on a free adjunct ('...after a sprain like this', '...in a new language') and two-part 'and what/or' questions where both parts are complete. Cut-off versions should end on a preposition, determiner, auxiliary or bare wh-word, so the model learns that missing arguments, not missing punctuation, are what signal unfinished.

patterns.name: Filler-heavy multi-clause turns that end in a question
patterns.explanation: Long disfluent turns ('uh', 'um', 'like', repeated commas, self-repairs) that give context and then end with a complete question are predicted unfinished, e.g. '...uh, can I just abort and start over', '...do I have to turn the pilot off too', 'do you uh, do you take walk-ins or do I need to um book ahead of time', '...is the big conference room on three free tomorrow from two to four, uh, for the board prep'. Fillers appear throughout these turns, so the model is wrongly treating them as a sign of continuation. What actually matters is the final clause, which is a complete interrogative.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~350 turns with 2-5 inserted fillers and comma pauses spread through the context part, ending in a complete yes/no, wh- or 'or' question with no '?' (topics: troubleshooting, appointments, bookings). Label them finished. For each one, make two unfinished siblings: one cut right after a filler inside the final question ('...so can I just um'), and one ending in a filler after the context but before any question ('...the service is running, uh,'). Also include self-repair questions ('do you uh, do you take...') that are finished once the repaired clause completes.

patterns.name: Short replies to a slot or confirmation prompt
patterns.explanation: Brief answers that fill a slot or confirm something, with no period, are predicted unfinished: 'yep it's under my name and the zip is 30318', 'alright yes to the first one and no to the second', 'okay sure go ahead and cancel it then', 'the window seat please and if possible somewhere toward the front of the plane', 'the name on the booking is Priya Raghunathan with an h right after the g', 'mhm yeah that's the exact charge I was calling about'. The model reads trailing modifiers, 'then', 'please' and coordinated answers as places where more could follow.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~300 dialogue-style answers (spelling clarifications, zip codes, yes/no to multiple items, seat or room preferences, 'go ahead and X then', 'put it under my work email not the personal one'), labelled finished with no final punctuation. Pair each with unfinished prefixes cut before the slot value ('the zip is', 'yes to the first one and', 'with an h right after the'). Include endings on 'then', 'please', 'instead', 'too' as finished markers.

patterns.name: Telegraphic commands and bare noun-phrase or fragment intents
patterns.explanation: Very short intents are predicted unfinished: 'Cancel Hulu', 'Talk to a human', 'Card declined', 'Switching to Verizon', 'I want it', 'two adults', 'Cancel my Spotify Premium'. The model seems to link short length with an incomplete fragment. But in customer-service and voice-agent settings, a verb + object command or a noun-phrase answer is a complete, actionable turn.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~250 two-to-five-word turns labelled finished: imperative + object ('Cancel Netflix', 'Speak to an agent', 'Reset my password'), event fragments ('Payment failed', 'Package missing', 'Moving to T-Mobile'), counts and quantities ('three adults', 'just one'), and pronoun-object statements ('I'll take it', 'I want that one'). Contrast them with unfinished short prefixes that lack a required object or complement ('Cancel my', 'Talk to a', 'I want to', 'Switching to', 'two adults and').

patterns.name: Unpunctuated formal or academic declaratives
patterns.explanation: Complete, well-formed sentences in formal register without a period are predicted unfinished: 'Im developing a framework to evaluate the effectiveness of these interventions', 'Experimental verification of topological insulator properties confirms theoretical predictions made decades earlier', 'Lets talk about our hobbies its a fun way to practice'. The model is relying on punctuation instead of checking whether the clause is syntactically closed (all arguments filled, no dangling conjunction or relative clause).
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~250 formal declaratives (research, business, language-learning topics) with no final punctuation and no apostrophes ('Im', 'its'), labelled finished. For each, add unfinished cuts at a determiner, preposition, complementizer or trailing conjunction ('...confirms theoretical predictions made', '...to evaluate the', '...but we need'). Also include sentences ending in a conditional or 'but'-clause that is itself complete ('...if practical challenges are overcome').

patterns.name: Long technical narrative declaratives chained with 'and'
patterns.explanation: Multi-clause technical explanations without a final period are predicted unfinished: 'I tried clearing the cache and reinstalling node modules twice and it still throws the same module not found error for lodash', 'we deploy with github actions to a kubernetes cluster on GKE and the image gets pushed to artifact registry right before the rollout', '...because it's getting a 500 instead of a 201'. The model treats repeated 'and'/'because' chaining and long length as a sign more is coming, even when the last clause is complete.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~250 developer and IT-support turns of 20-40 words with 2-4 'and'/'but'/'because'/'so' clauses, where the last clause is complete. Label them finished. For each, make unfinished siblings ending exactly on a dangling 'and', 'because', 'where we call', 'with the', or a mid-word cut ('artifact regis'). The goal: length and chaining are not signals; only the state of the final clause is.

patterns.name: Disfluent declaratives ending on a trailing modifier or sign-off
patterns.explanation: Rambling statements that end on an extra modifier or a closing discourse marker are predicted unfinished: '...like right by the uh old library', '...2:40 in the afternoon on the 12th', '...which is, uh, Navy Fed', '...but only when I lie down, okay', '...so yeah, that's it', '...no rush, fine'. A filler or comma right before the final phrase makes the model expect more. But closers like 'that's it', 'okay', 'fine' and complete add-on phrases explicitly mark the end of the turn.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~250 disfluent statements that end in (a) an explicit closer ('so yeah that's it', ', okay', ', fine', 'no rush', 'that's all') or (b) a filled-in modifier after a filler ('on, um, the 12th', 'which is, uh, Navy Fed'). Label them finished. Pair each with unfinished versions ending right on the filler or connector ('which is, uh,', 'lands at, um,', 'so yeah,') so the model learns the difference between a filler before a filled slot and a filler before an empty one.

patterns.name: Truncated content that is falsely closed (unfinished predicted finished)
patterns.explanation: Reverse errors: 'which is some facility in North Las.' has an ASR-emitted period on a word cut off mid-way (Las[Vegas]), and '...forty two Linden Street on the north side apartment' is missing the expected apartment number. The model trusts a final period or a sentence-shaped surface even when the last token is a broken proper noun or an expected value is missing.
patterns.data_recipe: Generate ~150 unfinished examples where the last word is a cut-off proper noun or common word followed by a spurious '.' or ',' ('in San Fran.', 'at the Walgr.', 'my account number is 44.'), and address or ID phrases ending on a slot-introducing noun with no value ('apartment', 'unit', 'suite', 'ending in', 'extension'). Pair each with the completed version labelled finished, so punctuation alone is never enough to call a turn finished.
